f.title: Operate pharmacovigilance and risk management systems

f.title: Submit all PSURs to the EU PSUR repository, not directly to the Authority
f.statement: MAHs are required to submit all PSURs to the central PSUR repository (mandatory since 13 June 2016 for centrally and nationally authorised products), via the eSubmission Gateway/Web Client, not directly to the Authority; for substances not on the EURD list, use the non-EU single assessment functionality.

f.title: Use signal and emerging safety issue channels for new safety information, not the PSUR
f.statement: Alternative mechanisms such as signal management and emerging safety issue channels should be used to communicate relevant new safety information to authorities.

rows.quote: Alternative mechanisms such as signal management and emerging safety issues channels should be used to communicate relevant new safety information to regulatory authorities

f.title: Keep product information up to date through variations
f.statement: MAHs are responsible for keeping product information up to date with current scientific knowledge, including EMA and national assessment conclusions and recommendations, by submitting appropriate variations.

rows.quote: It is the responsibility of Marketing Authorisation Holders to ensure that their product information is kept up-to-date in line with Article 16(3) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004/Article 23(3) of Directive 2001/83/EC by submitting the appropriate variations
rows.review_note: National (Malta) Medicines Authority guidance GL-PL03.10 (May 2025): national additions and national transposition (Pharmacovigilance Regulations 2012, S.L. 458.35) of EU duties; marked national. Review: quote proves the statement. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Pay the national PSUR fee and include proof of payment with the submission
f.statement: National PSUR assessment fee is EUR 2,300 payable to the Authority; a copy of the proof of payment must accompany the national PSUR submission (validation requirement), sent to the PSUR mailbox or placed in module m1\eu\10-cover\mt. MAHs must abide by PV standards including fees under Art 31A of the Medicines Act; non-compliance is an offence (Art 99).

f.title: PASS must not promote use; HCP payments limited to time and expenses
f.statement: When conducting non-interventional PASS/PAES, MAHs should ensure the study does not promote use of the product and payments to healthcare professionals are restricted to compensation for time and expenses.

rows.quote: The PASS does not promote the use of a medicinal product; • Payment to healthcare professionals for their participation should be restricted to the compensation for time and expenses incurred;

f.title: Submit the PASS final report to the Authority within 12 months of end of data collection
f.statement: For studies conducted in Malta, the final study report is submitted to the Authority within 12 months of the end of data collection unless a waiver is requested and accepted.

f.title: Monitor PASS data and communicate new benefit-risk information to all concerned authorities
f.statement: While the study runs the MAH shall monitor the data and consider benefit-risk implications; new information that might influence the benefit-risk balance must be communicated to the Authority and the competent authorities of Member States where the product is authorised.

rows.quote: While the study is being conducted, the marketing authorisation holder shall monitor the data generated and consider its implications on the benefit-risk balance of the medicinal product concerned
rows.review_note: National (Malta) Medicines Authority guidance GL-PL03.10 (May 2025): national additions and national transposition (Pharmacovigilance Regulations 2012, S.L. 458.35) of EU duties; marked national. Review: communication bullet read in text. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit imposed PASS draft protocol to the Authority (Malta only) or PRAC (several Member States)
f.statement: If a study is to be conducted only in Malta at the Authority's request under Article 22a, the MAH must submit a draft protocol to the Authority; if in more than one Member State, the protocol must be submitted to PRAC.

rows.quote: If a study is to be conducted only in Malta at the request of the Malta Medicines Authority according to Article 22a of Directive 2001/83/EC, the MAH must submit a draft protocol to the Malta Medicines Authority. If a study is to be conducted in more than 1 member state, then the MAH must submit the protocol to the Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee (PRAC).

f.title: Start the PASS only after endorsement and forward the protocol to other concerned Member States
f.statement: The study may only start after the MAH receives the endorsement letter from PRAC or the Authority; the MAH should then forward the protocol to the competent authorities of the other Member States where the study is conducted.

rows.quote: Commencement of the study may only take place when the MAH receives the letter of endorsement from the PRAC or the Malta Medicines Authority. When the letter of endorsement has been issued, the MAH should forward the protocol to the competent authorities of the other member states in which the study is to be conducted.

f.title: Submit substantial PASS protocol amendments before implementation and vary the MA per results
f.statement: Substantial protocol amendments should be submitted to the Authority or PRAC before implementation; depending on the study outcome the MAH should submit variations to the Authority and other competent authorities.

rows.quote: After commencement of the study, any substantial amendments to the protocol should be submitted to the Malta Medicines Authority or the PRAC before their implementation.

f.title: Acknowledge inspection notifications, name a contact and send pre-inspection documents on time
f.statement: On advance notification of an inspection, the MAH should acknowledge receipt, provide a contact person for inspection correspondence, and submit the pre-inspection documentation by the deadline given.

rows.deadline: By the deadline set for pre-inspection documentation
rows.quote: The MAH should initially acknowledge receipt of the notification and provide details of the relevant contact person for future correspondence about the inspection. f.title: Inform the Authority of a safety recall plan and send a reconciliation report afterwards
f.statement: For safety recalls the MAH should inform the Authority of its coordinated recall plan (action plan and timelines, DHPC, details of stopping supply to wholesalers or pharmacies, letters to pharmacies and wholesalers) and send a reconciliation report after the recall.

rows.quote: The MAH should inform the Malta Medicines Authority about its coordinated plan to carry out the recall;

f.title: Art 126a holders: keep full PV obligations, ADR reporting and SOPs to pass ADRs to the MAH
f.statement: Article 126a authorisation holders have no pharmacovigilance waiver. They must have a system to report ADRs to EudraVigilance; holders that are not the MAH (e.g. wholesalers) without EudraVigilance access should have SOPs to transmit ADRs to the MAH abroad. They may have a PSMF.

f.title: Art 126a holders: screen Commission decisions and have SOPs to implement RMMs, DHPCs and recalls
f.statement: Article 126a holders must have a quality system to identify products with RMMs to implement, including screening of Commission decisions and SOPs for implementing RMMs and DHPCs, and a safety recall system at the distributor.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote: Group 1 and 2 authorisation holders must have a quality system on how to identify that their products have got RMMs to be implemented. Thus a method of screening community decisions is required as well as SOPs in place for implementing RMMs and DHPCs.

f.title: Parallel importers: have systems for ADR forwarding to the MAH, safety recalls and RMM/DHPC implementation
f.statement: Parallel importers must have at least a system to identify and send ADRs to the MAH, a safety recall system and a system to implement RMMs and DHPCs. Before placing a PI product on the Maltese market they should request all associated RMM materials from the MAH and, alone or with the MAH, comply with RMM distribution.

rows.quote: However, they must have at least: a) A system to identify and send ADRs to the MAH, who then has to comply with pharmacovigilance legislations and comply with Directive 2001/83/EC obligations b) A system of safety recalls c) A system to implement RMMs/DHPCs

f.title: Enter authorised products in XEVMPD with the correct MAH; sponsors enter all IMPs
f.statement: Each MAH should enter in XEVMPD the information on products for which it holds a marketing authorisation, specifying the MAH per the granted authorisation; sponsors must enter all IMPs studied in EEA clinical trials.

f.title: Hospital-exemption ATMPs: apply PV standards equivalent to centrally authorised ATMPs
f.statement: Manufacture of ATMPs under the hospital exemption must be authorised by the Authority, and traceability, quality and pharmacovigilance standards must be equivalent to centrally authorised ATMPs, including follow-up of efficacy and adverse reactions and risk management.

f.statement: MAHs, wholesalers, parallel importers and Art 126(a) holders are encouraged to use dedicated ADR forms going beyond the four minimum elements: start/stop dates, patient characteristics, relevant laboratory tests, concomitant medicines, dechallenge/rechallenge, ongoing status and free-text narrative; forms should be clear and easy to use.

f.title: Have SOPs for ADR management, follow-up, targeted questionnaires, documentation and duplicate prevention
f.statement: There should be SOPs standardising ADR management, defining when and how often to request follow-up, using targeted follow-up questionnaires for RMP safety concerns where needed, documenting all follow-up attempts, and preventing duplicate reports.

f.title: Apply a four-eye check, train data-entry staff and manage E2B data quality
f.statement: Implement a multiple-eye (e.g. four-eye) verification of ADR data entry, provide regular training to data-entry and ADR staff, and ensure systems transmit high-quality data to EudraVigilance within legal timeframes (e.g. correct use of C.1.4/C.1.5 and E.i.8, consistent fields, accurate MedDRA coding, no duplicates).
